clue.text: Warning Lord Verulam about starting "Essays"

indicators.note: about means the title is placed around the other piece

parts.note: Francis Bacon, author of the Essays, was created Baron Verulam

indicators.note: starting picks out only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone warns the philosopher Bacon as he begins writing his Essays.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon was Baron Verulam, and he did write Essays, which makes the surface feel like literary history. 'about' puts BACON around E, the first letter of 'Essays'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal fire lit to give a warning of danger.

clue.text: One of enquiring nature, formerly a collier

parts.note: ex- means former
a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: An inquisitive person who used to work down a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who asks questions to test or inspect is an inquirer.

clue.text: A business centre has better, superior position

indicators.note: superior means placed higher, so in this down clue it sits on top of the rest

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A commercial hub enjoys the edge, being in a lofty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London is its financial district. 'superior' puts CAP above A and CITY in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A capacity is a role or post, as in acting in an official capacity.

clue.text: Modern artist established near Dungeness

parts.note: new means modern
George Romney was an 18th-century English portrait painter

explanation.surface: A contemporary painter has set up home on the Kent coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Dungeness is a headland on the Kent coast; the town in question is close by.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cinque Port town stands a few miles from that shingle headland in Kent.

clue.text: Idle creature on the other side

parts.note: a tick is a small blood-sucking creature
over can mean across, on the far side

explanation.surface: A lazy animal is lounging across the way.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over runs slowly without doing work, so the verb means to idle.

clue.text: Event for Manxmen?

parts.note: the Isle of Man's emblem shows three legs joined together, so a Manxman is pictured with that many legs

explanation.definitionFit: A sports-day race where partners run with two of their legs tied together.

clue.text: Dishonesty shown up in American Revolution

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the assembled piece is read upwards, backwards
in puts the revolution inside the American

parts.note: a Yank is an American
rev is short for revolution, as in engine revs

explanation.surface: Fraud was exposed during the War of Independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' is a reversal signal in a down clue; 'Revolution' looks like the war of 1775 but is just the abbreviation for an engine revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavery is roguish, deceitful conduct.

clue.text: In fine fettle, I agree

explanation.surface: Someone in good health assents.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in good health, and is also a reply of consent such as 'all right then'.

clue.text: Turning corrupt, a politician

parts.note: to rot is to corrupt or decay
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP goes bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory means revolving, spinning round an axis.

clue.text: The people available to plough, reap 'n' mow

indicators.note: to plough is to turn the soil over, so these letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A farm needs workers to plough, reap and mow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plough' looks like farm work beside reaping and mowing, but it is the anagram signal for REAPNMOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Manpower is the workforce, the number of workers one can call on.

clue.text: Make a mistake in quotation about the Upper House

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole assembled piece is read backwards
in places the mistake inside the quotation

parts.note: a tag is a familiar quotation
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone misquotes a remark concerning the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TERRAG, the result of ERR placed in TAG. 'the Upper House' suggests the House of Lords; it means the topmost part of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A garret is an attic room right at the top of a building.

clue.text: Publish the record that has to be beaten

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
to lose is to be beaten in a contest

explanation.surface: An athlete sets a world record that rivals must now beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to reveal or make known, much as one makes news public.

clue.text: Plover's cry echoed by it

parts.note: the bird is named after its call, whose second syllable rhymes with 'it'

explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, a kind of plover, is called after its two-note cry.

clue.text: Bent copper's lead a number refuse to accept

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: to accept means to take another piece inside

parts.note: to deny is to refuse

indicators.note: lead picks the first letter, the one that goes in front

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman's tip-off is something several people refuse to take up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as crooked, describing the copper, but it is the definition. 'to accept' puts C, the first letter of 'copper's', inside DENY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination, a leaning towards something.

clue.text: One who can sing very loudly in church after tea

indicators.note: after puts the tea in front of the rest

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A chorister belts out hymns once tea is over.
explanation.definitionFit: This common finch is a songbird.

clue.text: Sue leads pupils running after you

indicators.note: the leads of these words are their first letters, the ones at the front

explanation.surface: A girl called Sue heads a group of schoolchildren racing behind you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a name; it is the verb, to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue can mean to beg or entreat, as in suing for peace.

clue.text: Ingots about to become waste

parts.note: pigs are oblong ingots of cast metal, as in pig iron
will marks what is going to happen

explanation.surface: Bars of metal are on the point of being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is kitchen scraps fed to pigs.

clue.text: Certify doctor has left democratic organization

indicators.note: organization means arranging, so the remaining letters are put into order

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A physician quits a political body and vouches for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has left' takes MO out of DEMOCRATIC; 'organization' rearranges what remains, DECRATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit is to give official recognition or authorise.

clue.text: Join everybody in the lead to July 4th

indicators.note: in the lead to means the first piece goes in front of the second

parts.note: everybody means all

indicators.note: 4th picks the fourth letter of the word July

explanation.surface: Everyone is invited to join the parade on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'July 4th' suggests the American holiday; it is the fourth letter of 'July'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to unite or combine with another party.

clue.text: Booth, for instance, has two animals inside

indicators.note: two means the word for the animal appears twice over

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
inside means within, and in is its short form

explanation.surface: A stall at a fair holds a pair of donkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booth' suggests a stall; it is John Wilkes Booth, who shot President Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wilkes Booth killed Abraham Lincoln, an example of a political murderer.

clue.text: Sole means of communication left to one cat

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: A last link to the outside world is bequeathed to a single cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or channel that is someone's only link to help or contact.

clue.text: Used by Peter Wimsey, sagely, to move from point to point

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: to move means the letters of the word sagely are shifted into a new order

parts.note: S, south, is another compass point

explanation.surface: The detective Lord Peter Wimsey wisely strolls from place to place.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy L. Sayers's detective Lord Peter Wimsey wears a monocle. 'to move' shuffles the letters of 'sagely'; 'from point to point' puts the result between two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A single eyeglass, a monocle, is the trademark accessory of the fictional aristocrat sleuth.

clue.text: English sailors wearing duck that never wears out

indicators.note: wearing means the sailors have the duck around them

parts.note: a teal is a kind of duck
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: English seamen dressed in tough cotton cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' suggests the hard-wearing cloth that sailors wore; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means everlasting, without end.

clue.text: World covered by solid ice

indicators.note: covered by puts the first piece inside the second

parts.note: set means solid, firm
an orb is a globe, a world

explanation.surface: The globe is encased in a frozen layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a water ice, a frozen dessert.

clue.text: Settled quarrel indeed!

annotationWithheld.why: Settled quarrel indeed! — the parse is FRAY in DEED, reading 'indeed' as 'in deed', so the word 'indeed' is both the container signal 'in' and the letters DEED; one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Cut order

explanation.surface: A two-word instruction to make an incision.
explanation.definitionFit: An indent is a notch cut into an edge, and also an official requisition for goods.

clue.text: "We can't know" he says, "what makes acting so funny"

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of acting so are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A doubter quips about what makes stage performance amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'funny', on the letters ACTINGSO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic holds that the existence of God cannot be known.

clue.text: In general, stock of cards is much less

indicators.note: In means the cards are put inside the name of the general

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
in card games the talon is the undealt stock

explanation.surface: Generally the number of cards held in reserve is far smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'generally', but 'In' is the container signal and 'general' is LEE. In card games the talon is the pile of undealt cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means 'still less', as in 'I can't walk, much less run'.

clue.text: Long yarn about retirement

parts.note: a hank is a coil of yarn

indicators.note: retirement means a drawing back, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale is told concerning someone leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a story; it is wool. 'retirement' reverses RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To hanker is to yearn or crave, as to long is.
